faqs.question: What is the Zeiss Smart Zoom 5 used for?
faqs.answer: It's an automated digital microscope for quality assurance, quality control, and failure analysis across industrial applications, built to be simple enough for untrained users while delivering reproducible results.

faqs.question: What is the magnification range?
faqs.answer: 10x to 2020x, across four smart objectives.

faqs.question: What happens when an objective is changed mid-inspection?
faqs.answer: The objectives are encoded, so the software automatically recognizes the change, recalibrates measurement, and returns to the correct focus and x/y position, no manual refocusing or relocation needed.

faqs.question: Does it protect the sample from accidental contact?
faqs.answer: Yes, collision detection automatically retracts the optical engine to a safe position the instant contact is detected, protecting both the sample and the user.

faqs.question: Can repeat inspections be automated?
faqs.answer: Yes, macro recording mode stores step-by-step workflows for the same sample type, letting them be repeated reproducibly without in-depth microscope knowledge.

faqs.question: What is the Best Image function?
faqs.answer: A one-click feature that generates a series of images under varying lighting and processing conditions, including HDR, noise filtering, and sharpening, so the best result can be selected for the application.

faqs.question: Can Smart Zoom 5 connect to an electron microscope?
faqs.answer: Yes, through Shuttle & Find, which relocates a defined region of interest from the digital microscope to an electron microscope using automated marker recognition, then aligns both images into an overlay.

faqs.question: What illumination options are available?
faqs.answer: A built-in, segmentable LED ring light, giving complete control over illumination, alongside coaxial brightfield and full or segmented ringlight configurations demonstrated across various applications.

faqs.question: Does tilting the microscope lose the region of interest?
faqs.answer: No, the motorized, encoded architecture keeps the focused region of interest in focus and centered even as the arm tilts up to ±45°.

faqs.question: Can reports be generated directly?
faqs.answer: Yes, images can be annotated and exported directly to Word report templates.

faqs.question: How is Smart Zoom 5 different from Zeiss's research microscopes?
faqs.answer: Smart Zoom 5 belongs to Zeiss's Industrial Quality Solutions division, built specifically for QA/QC, failure analysis, and industrial inspection with encoded, automated optics. The Research Microscopy Solutions range (Primostar, Axiovert, Stemi, SteREO Discovery) is built for biological and life science research instead.

longForm.heroHook: Swap the objective. It refocuses, recalibrates, and finds the exact spot on its own.
longForm.heroLead: Changing magnification usually means losing your place, refocus, relocate, recalibrate, repeat. Smart Zoom 5 removes that entirely. Every objective is encoded, so the moment it's swapped, the software recognizes the change, corrects the measurement calibration, and returns to the exact focus and x/y position, no manual recovery step required. Four smart objectives cover a 10x to 2020x magnification range, with a built-in, segmentable LED ring light giving complete control over illumination. Collision detection retracts the optical engine automatically the instant an objective contacts the sample, protecting both in one motion. Built-in vibration dampening and optical image stabilization keep detail crisp even on a busy industrial floor. A macro recording mode captures a step-by-step inspection workflow once, then repeats it reproducibly, without needing microscope expertise from whoever runs it next. And when a defect needs a closer look under an electron microscope, Shuttle & Find relocates the exact region of interest there in the shortest possible time, no manual re-searching required. What it removes: manual refocusing, recalibration, and relocation on every objective change. What it protects: both the sample and the operator, automatically, on contact. What it connects to: an electron microscope, when the inspection needs to go further.

sections.title: Encoded Objectives, Explained
sections.description: Why swapping lenses doesn't cost setup time here.
body: Changing magnification on most microscopes means losing everything the inspection had already established, focus, calibration, and exactly where on the sample the region of interest actually was. Every swap becomes a small reset, refocus manually, recalibrate manually, hunt for the same spot manually.

Smart Zoom 5's objectives are encoded, so the system knows exactly which one is mounted at all times. Swap objectives mid-inspection, and the software recognizes the change immediately: measurement calibration adjusts automatically, focus returns to where it was, and the x/y position snaps back to the exact region of interest, ready to continue the analysis without any of the usual recovery steps.

sections.title: Shuttle & Find
sections.description: How a region of interest moves from digital to electron microscopy. Some failure analysis needs more resolution than any optical microscope can provide, and the usual bridge to an electron microscope is manual: describe the location, hope it translates, spend real time re-finding the same spot under a completely different imaging system. Shuttle & Find removes that gap. Define a region of interest on Smart Zoom 5, and the same location relocates on the electron microscope within the shortest possible time, using automated marker recognition rather than manual searching. Once found, both images align into a single overlay, giving a direct visual bridge between the optical and electron-level views of the exact same feature. Share whether the failure analysis workflow already includes electron microscopy, and Shuttle & Find compatibility gets confirmed against your existing SEM setup.

faqs.question: What is the Zeiss Axio Zoom V16 used for?
faqs.answer: It's a fluorescence stereo zoom microscope built for large object fields, used to image complete model organisms in fluorescence contrast, alongside routine screening and demanding multidimensional imaging.

faqs.question: What is the zoom ratio?
What numerical aperture does it achieve?
faqs.answer: NA 0.25 as the stated headline figure, reaching NA 0.5 with the Plan-NEOFLUAR Z 2.3x objective across a 1.5 mm object field, already in the medium zoom range.

faqs.question: Can it image whole organisms in fluorescence?
faqs.answer: Yes, demonstrated directly on a complete mouse embryo and a two-color Drosophila embryo, without needing to tile or stitch multiple fields.

faqs.question: What are the three zoom modes?
faqs.answer: Brightness mode (highest brightness across the zoom range, for fluorescence), Eyepiece mode (optimized for ocular observation), and Camera mode (adapted to the connected camera's performance).

faqs.question: What does the Best Mode button do?
faqs.answer: It determines the current optical state and automatically optimizes transmitted light, including an increased-contrast brightfield option, and can save and reload that configuration for future experiments.

faqs.question: What is eZoom?
faqs.answer: An electronic zoom system that replaces the mechanical zoom curve with stepping motors, correcting for individual lens tolerances and delivering doubled precision compared to a mechanical zoom body.

faqs.question: How is it controlled?
faqs.answer: Via a SyCop 3 touchscreen, consistent with the control approach used across the SteREO Discovery family.

faqs.question: How does it fit into Zeiss's wider stereo and zoom range?
faqs.answer: It shares modular system interfaces with SteREO Discovery V8, V12, and V20, all documented together in Zeiss's stereo and zoom microscope family profile.

faqs.question: How is it different from SteREO Discovery V20?
faqs.answer: Both use eZoom, but V16 is built specifically around fluorescence brightness and large object fields for whole-organism imaging, while V20 is built for maximum stereo magnification (up to 345x) and highly reproducible zoom positioning.

sections.title: Product Information
sections.description: Discover how the ZEISS Axio Zoom V16 combines high numerical aperture, large-field fluorescence imaging, and intelligent zoom automation for advanced biological research.
body: A 16x zoom combined with a numerical aperture of NA 0.25. Positioned at the forefront of known stereo and zoom microscopes, per Zeiss.
Very high aperture achieved already in the medium zoom range. Not reserved for the extreme top end of magnification.
Superior brightness in large object fields. Complete model organisms viewed in fluorescence contrast, not fragmented.
NA 0.5 with the Plan-NEOFLUAR Z 2.3x objective. Across a 1.5 mm object field.
Supports routine screening and demanding multidimensional imaging. Both, in the medium zoom range, without needing to push to maximum magnification.
eZoom pairs a motorized iris diaphragm with the zoom. Three selectable modes optimize for the actual task.
Brightness mode holds highest possible brightness across the full zoom range. For fluorescence observation.
Eyepiece mode favors conventional ocular observation. Maximum depth of field at large fields, maximum resolution at high magnification.
Camera mode adapts to the connected camera's performance. Optimal resolution-to-depth-of-field balance across the whole zoom range.
Increased-contrast brightfield available at the touch of the Best Mode button. Alongside standard brightfield, darkfield, and oblique illumination.
The system determines the actual optical state and optimizes transmitted light automatically. No manual calculation required.
Settings save and reload at the touch of a button. The exact configuration returns for the next experiment.
eZoom replaces the mechanical zoom curve with an electronic one. Stepping motors position lenses precisely, accounting for individual lens tolerances.
Each zoom body describes its own zoom curve. Rather than one mechanical curve applied uniformly across every unit.
Doubled precision compared to a mechanical zoom body. Visibly more captured detail across the magnification range.
Controlled via SyCop 3 touchscreen. The same control philosophy carried through the SteREO Discovery family.
Part of the same modular system as SteREO Discovery V8, V12, and V20. Shared interfaces and adapters across the full stereo and zoom range.

sections.eyebrow: Three Zoom Modes, One Purpose Each
sections.title: Three Zoom Modes, One Purpose Each
sections.description: Why the same optical path behaves differently depending on what's actually happening.
body: Every stereo zoom microscope balances the same three things against each other, brightness, depth of field, and resolution, and the ideal balance shifts depending on whether someone's looking through the eyepieces, capturing a camera image, or chasing the brightest possible fluorescence signal. Axio Zoom V16 doesn't force one fixed compromise across all three, eZoom's motorized iris diaphragm shifts the balance per mode.

Brightness mode holds the highest possible brightness across the entire zoom range, built specifically for fluorescence observation where signal strength is the whole game. Eyepiece mode favors conventional ocular observation, maximum depth of field at large fields for orientation, maximum resolution at high magnification for detail. Camera mode adapts to whatever camera is actually connected, tuning the resolution-to-depth-of-field relationship to get the most out of that specific sensor across the full range.

sections.title: Intelligent Transmitted Light
sections.description: What the Best Mode button actually automates. Manually optimizing transmitted light for a given specimen and zoom position means understanding the current optical state well enough to adjust it correctly, a skill that takes real time to build and doesn't transfer automatically to a different operator. The Best Mode button removes that requirement. Axio Zoom V16 determines the actual optical state on its own and optimizes transmitted light automatically, adding increased-contrast brightfield to the standard brightfield, darkfield, and oblique options already available. Once the setting is right for a specific application, it saves and reloads at the touch of the same button, so the next experiment starts from exactly the same optical configuration rather than being rebuilt from scratch.
